findings.title: Ceiling recovery targets the pass PID, not the over-ceiling worker
findings.specimen: attavo/doctor.py::write_invocation_marker records os.getpid() before attavo/drive.py::_start_stage spawns the detached worker; attavo/drive.py::_recover_one later sends SIGTERM to that marker PID. The worker can therefore survive a ceiling recovery and subsequently write a competing record.
findings.retires: The claim that stage ceilings terminate workers, rather than merely recording them as hung while their work continues.
findings.severity: Harmless only when the worker has already exited independently; blocking when an alive worker crosses its ceiling and continues running after recovery.

findings.title: Recovered retry attempts lose retry_of and steer provenance
findings.specimen: attavo/drive.py::_recover_one unconditionally writes "retry_of": null and "steer": null, including for build-02/verify-02 markers started as retries. This contradicts the required record shape for every retried attempt.
findings.retires: Ambiguous recovered records that cannot identify the prior attempt or the counsel steer whose input they consumed.
findings.severity: Harmless for a first attempt; blocking when attempt 02 or later dies or hangs and its recovered record omits its retry lineage.

findings.title: Exhaustion caused by recovery never receives the required final counsel read
findings.specimen: attavo/drive.py::_stage_body invokes counsel after an ordinarily completed non-pass record exhausts the budget, but attavo/drive.py::_recover_one commits died/hung records directly and never invokes counsel. Two identical recovered failures therefore stop early without the exhaustion sentence required beside the comparison.
findings.retires: Exhaustion reports that present only mechanical attempt comparison and omit counsel’s final interpretation.
findings.severity: Harmless while recovery leaves retry budget available; blocking when a recovered died or hung record spends the budget or triggers the identical-signature early stop.

findings.title: Questions are retried after counsel answer despite being explicitly non-retryable
findings.specimen: attavo/drive.py::NEVER_RETRIED_CLASSES omits question, and retry_state consequently starts another attempt when counsel answers one. tests/test_retry.py::test_counsels_verdict_routes_the_next_pass positively encodes this divergence even though the approved spec and build commit both say a question is never retried by this item.
findings.retires: Automatic reruns after a stop whose answer may alter or interpret the definition of done.
findings.severity: Harmless when no counsel answer exists; blocking when a question receives an answer and the next pass automatically starts another attempt.

findings.title: --again bypasses person-only stops, not just exhausted retry budgets
findings.specimen: attavo/drive.py::_pass_once calls _advance_again for every stopped state that is neither presently eligible nor waiting. Thus --again can restart claims-boundary, environment, gate, unanswered/person-ruled question, and patch stops, although the approved narrowing permits it only after a stage’s retry budget or early stop is spent.
findings.retires: The old broad --again escape hatch inside states reserved for an operator or later breaker behavior.
findings.severity: Harmless without --again; blocking when --again is issued against a person-only or never-retried stop and creates a new marker.
